source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 is span 3, max height 2, two scramble steps, one excess voxel, no relief, and 60000 ms cooling.
Both full and simplified surfaces are implemented; full uses drags, simplified uses proxy clicks/buttons, and the configured observation window is 600 ms with one frame.
Draw and upset move one voxel only when their height predicates hold; split discards one voxel, and none of these changes occurs without an action.

The target and scrambled initial solid are generated statically, and solution is explicitly the reversed smithing route plus split actions; the world sets cooling_ms, heat_ms=2400, workable=0.35, and initial_heat=1.0.
thermal() decays heat on the anvil and raises it in the forge; strike rejects cold, forge-located, empty, or blocked contacts and changes heights only on a strike event.
The heat meter/label is rendered, simplified mode binds clicks/buttons, full mode binds hammer/tongs/orbit drags, and an 80 ms paint interval performs the thermal repaint.
The workable heat meter and forge state are visibly rendered.
The grader replays heat from event timestamps and location, checks the workable threshold, and applies voxel changes only for replayed strikes.
A final stamp is required and success is h==target with material conservation; the grader does not autonomously complete the solid.
The wiring solver performs each private-route strike, explicitly transfers to the forge when TOO COLD, waits for reheating, returns to the anvil, and stamps.
